subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw add a core enforced execution-progress contract for artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and post-green follow-through, or should this stay limited to existing loop/stale-run guardrails plus smaller bug fixes?
rationale: The request is aligned with runtime reliability, but it adds new enforcement policy, persistence, config, and telemetry surface that could change user-visible agent behavior and needs maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core guardrail design
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker and require a scoped MVP that reuses runner/diagnostic events, SQLite state, and measured telemetry before enabling enforcement.

options.title: Narrow to existing guardrails
options.body: Split only concrete bugs into smaller issues against tool-loop, stale-run, and timeout detectors, and defer artifact-gated status enforcement until live traces justify it.

options.title: Decline broad enforcement
options.body: Close this direction as too policy-heavy for core and continue relying on opt-in loop detection, post-compaction guards, and operator monitoring.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core guardrail design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker and require a scoped MVP that reuses runner/diagnostic events, SQLite state, and measured telemetry before enabling enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the best available routing candidate from current history for recent agent runtime/release guardrail surfaces, though original loop detection ownership is shared.
